title: Flask
wikitext:
A '''flask''' is a rechargeable potion. When used, the flask consumes a certain amount of flask charges and [[Recovery|recovers]] a portion of [[life]], [[mana]] or grants temporary bonuses for the duration of the flask effect. 

__TOC__

==Flask types==
Flasks are a category of [[item class]]es that includes [[life flask]]s, [[mana flask]]s, [[hybrid flask]]s and [[utility flask]]s. The primary effect of life flasks, mana flasks and hybrid flasks is the recovery of [[life]], [[mana]] or both, respectively. These types of flasks can be referred to as recovery flasks. The primary effect of utility flasks applies bonus [[modifiers]] to the character. Each utility flask grants a different [[stat]].

{| class="wikitable"
! Flask type
! Primary effect
|-
| [[Life flask]]
| Recovers life
|-
| [[Mana flask]]
| Recovers mana
|-
| [[Hybrid flask]]
| Recovers life and mana
|-
| [[Utility flask]]
| Grants bonus effect

==Mechanics==
[[File:Flask inventory.png|thumb|right|A player's flask inventory.]]

Every [[character]] has space for five flasks. When the player enters a town or a [[hideout]], all of their flasks are automatically fully recharged. If a player equips a flask within a hostile area, the flask has zero active charges by default.

Flasks can only be {{c|normal|normal}}, {{c|magic|magic}} or {{c|unique|unique}}. There are no {{c|rare|rare}} flasks. 

===Flask charges===
Flasks store different amount of charges and spend different amount per sip depending on flask type. These parameters can be altered with [[modifier]]s on equipment, [[Flask#Modifiers|flasks]] and [[passive skill]]s. The amount of charges gained from any sources can be altered with modifiers {{c|mod|#% increased/reduced Flask Charges gained}} (e.g. from equipment and passive skills) and {{c|mod|#% increased/reduced Charge Recovery}} (e.g. from the "Perpetual" flask prefix). These modifiers stack multiplicatively. Partial charges are tracked with at least two decimals, though not displayed for the player.
 
Flask charges can be gained in several ways: 
* by killing enemies; a {{c|normal|normal}} monster grants 1 charge, a {{c|magic|magic}} monster grants 3.5 charges, a {{c|rare|rare}} monster grants 6 charges, and a {{c|unique|unique}} monster grants 11 charges.<ref name="MechanicsThread"/> Monsters in acts 6 to 10 generate fewer flask charges and monsters in maps generate even fewer still.<ref name ="ExpeditionGameBalance"/>
* Modifiers indicating "{{c|mod|Flasks gain # charge(s) every # seconds}}", such as the ones from [[Pathfinder]]'s passive [[Nature's Adrenaline]], [[The Traitor (keystone passive)]], {{il|Alchemist's Mark}} and the [[Searing Exarch implicit modifier]], recover that many charges to all your equipped flasks.
* [[Critical strike]]s may generate flask charges through {{c|mod|(% chance to) gain a Flask Charge when you deal a Critical Strike}}. This effect grants one charge to one flask<ref>[[Version 2.5.0#Flask_Charge_Generation_on_Critical_Strike]]</ref>, with a single cooldown shared between all effects, local and global. While this cooldown is stated to be 0.1s<ref>[[Version 3.13.0#Character_Balance]]</ref>, it is functionally 0.132s due to the game's 0.033s server frames, limiting charge gain to ~7.5 per second.<ref>https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_OcsO9rgJDc</ref> It is not affected by {{c|mod|#% increased Cooldown Recovery Rate}}.

Within a party, all players close to the killed enemy gain charges.<ref name="MarkPartyFlaskCharges"/>

===Recovery from flasks===
Certain flasks [[Recovery|recover]] [[life]] and/or [[mana]] over time. Flasks end their respective effects if maximum life or mana is reached. [[Hybrid flask]]s, which affect both life and mana, will end their effects if both life and mana are fully recovered. Recovery flasks queue up if multiple flasks are active. The effect with the highest regeneration rate is always applied first.<ref name="MechanicsThread"/>

There are 4 parameters that affect recovery from flasks:
* {{c|mod|#% increased/reduced Amount Recovered}} causes a flask to recover an increased/reduced amount. The duration is unchanged.<ref name="MarkFlaskEffect" />
* {{c|mod|#% increased/reduced Recovery Speed/Rate}} causes a flask to recover the same total amount at a faster/slower rate.<ref name="FlaskRecoveryRate" /> 
* {{c|mod|Instant Recovery}} cause a flask to restore the whole amount instantly by overriding the duration to 0.
* {{c|mod|Flask effect is not removed when Unreserved Mana is Filled}} causes a flask to not end its effect when the user recovers to maximum mana.

Modifiers to flask effect apply to recovery from flasks, multiplicatively with increased recovery from flasks as well as flask quality. Modifiers to {{c|mod|Flask effect duration}} increase the duration of the flask without decreasing the amount recovered per second, effectively acting as a multiplier to amount recovered, if the flask recovery is not instant. 

===Effects of flasks===
Flask effects are temporary effects created by using flasks. Life and mana recovery flask effects have no icon, but other flask effects can be identified by icons with a gold border.<ref name="MarkBuffs"/> Flask effects behave similarly to [[buff]]s, but are not classified as [[buff]]s for relevant effects (see [[active and temporary effects]]).

Effects of flasks as well as their durations can be increased with several flask modifiers, [[#Passive skills|passive skills]] and [[equipment]].

Timed immunities granted by flasks (e.g. {{c|mod|Grants Immunity to Bleeding for # seconds if used while Bleeding}}) are not considered flask effects for the purpose of e.g. {{c|mod|#% increased Elemental Damage during any Flask Effect}}. 

When creating multiple of the same (non-recovery) flask effect, each effect has an independent duration, and only the strongest applies. 

{{cot|Example: activating multiple flasks}}
Example: Say you have a 
* {{il|Jade Flask}} (duration 5s) with +20% movement speed.
* {{il|Ruby Flask}} (duration 3.5s) modified with +30% movement speed.
* {{il|Granite Flask}} (duration 4s) with +100% armour. 
If you activate the jade flask initially, you get a +20% movement speed bonus. If 0.5 seconds later you activate the ruby flask, you will then have +30% movement speed – the original 20% movement speed effect still has 4.5 seconds left, but is overwritten by the stronger effect temporarily. If 0.5 seconds later you activate your granite flask, then you have +30% movement speed and +100% armour. The armour and movement speed mods are different suffixes, so they don't conflict – they will stack together. 3 seconds later your ruby flask effect ends, but the jade flask still has 1 second left, so you revert to the +20% movement speed from the jade flask until it expires.
{{cob}}

===Quality===
{{Main|Quality}}

{{il|Glassblower's Bauble|Glassblower's Baubles}} are used to increase the quality of a flask up to 20%. Quality on recovery flasks increases the amount of life and/or mana recovered by that percentage. Utility flasks gain increased duration instead. Note that quality on flasks stacks multiplicatively with other modifiers to flasks (for example, the increased flask duration nodes from the passive tree or belts). Furthermore, things with increased flask effect will not only improve the implicit mod of a flask, but any of the mods that the flask has rolled (always rounded down).

Flasks can be corrupted using a {{il|Vaal Orb}} to gain -10 to +10 quality at random, exceeding the 20% default maximum. [[List_of_monster_reward_mods|Monster reward modifiers]] can cause flasks to drop with up to 30% quality uncorrupted, which can be corrupted to increase its quality to up to 40%.

===Instilling Orb===
{{il|Instilling Orb}} gives a utility flask an implicit modifier which causes the flask to be automatically used when a certain condition is met. You can still activate the flask manually.

===Enkindling Orb===
{{il|Enkindling Orb}} grants a utility flask an implicit modifier that improves the flask, but causes the flask to not gain charges while it's active.

==Interactions==
===Flask Charge Drain===
The [[monster modifier]] "Siphons Flask Charges" causes nearby players to lose 6 flask charges every 3 seconds.

Searing Exarch [[Eldritch Altar]]s can have {{c|mod|Enemies lose 6 Flask Charges every 3 seconds and cannot gain Flask Charges for 6 seconds after being Hit}} as a downside effect on bosses and Eldritch minions.

In [[The Lord's Labyrinth|Eternal Labyrinths]], an Endless Drought Sentinel Trap drains flask charges when it hits a nearby player.

Utility flasks can be enchanted by spending {{il|Instilling Orb}} or {{il|Enkindling Orb}}

|where=mods.domain=1 AND mod_stats.id LIKE "%flask%" AND mods.generation_type IN ( "21", "22" )

|generation_type=1
}}

==Vendor recipes==
Divine and eternal life and mana flasks can '''not''' be obtained from the flask progression.

The developers stated in the forum that the vendor recipe chain on life and mana flasks was intended to stop with divine flasks.<ref name="HenryVendorDivine" /> This seems to extend to buying them with sanctified ones.

}}

* Rebalanced most of the mods on flasks around the new behavioural changes. 
* "Low Life" on Cautious flasks is now defined as 35% rather than 50%, to be consistent with other uses of the term. 
}}
